messages.subject: Re:
messages.body_plain:
I admit that we've not created sufficient tools to make
proper use of the scanqtl() results.  It's on my list of
things to do.

I'd definitely recommend taking account of all inferred loci
when doing the 2d scan on chromosome 11.  If you have fully
typed markers near the inferred QTLs, you can pull out the
genotype data for those and use them as additive covariates
in scantwo.

scantwo() has an argument "chr" that you can use to do the
2d scan on only selected chromosomes.  Alternatively, you can
use subset(mycross, chr=11) to create a cross object with
just the chromosome 11 genotype data.

karl

messages.subject: Re: get.ests in fitqtl
messages.body_plain:
I responded directly to the author on this one, but it seems I should
respond back to the group as well, in case anyone else is interested.

It appears that fitqtl() cannot handle interactions among covariates;
those must be set up in advance.  We must then also include the
relevant covariates and interactions in the formula.
So, if I want to include an age x sex interaction, I need to do
something like the following:

  ac <- mycross$pheno[,c("age","sex")]
  ac <- cbind(ac, sex.by.age=ac[,1]*ac[,2])

  out.fitqtl<-fitqtl(mycross$pheno[,1], qtl, formula = y ~ Q1 + Q2 +
                     + age + sex + sex.by.age + Q2*age + Q2*sex +
                     Q2*sex.by.age,
                     cov = ac, get.ests=TRUE)

Also, there was a bug in fitqtl() regarding the naming of coefficients
for covariate-by-QTL interactions.  I have a fix for that; email me if
you need it. I hope to release a new version within a month or so,
which will include the fix (plus other things).

karl

messages.body_plain:
Here again, I responded directly to the author, but thought I should
also respond to the group, on the off chance that someone else is
interested.

I slightly modified the function read.cross.csv() so that it will work
with 4-way cross data.  Email me to get the revised code, or wait until
the next release of the software.

To read in 4-way cross data, you need to do something like the
following:

   x <- read.cross("csv", "", "4waycross.csv", genotypes=NULL)

"genotypes=NULL" tells the function to not modify the genotype codes,
which must be set up within the file.

karl

messages.subject: Re: Frequency distributions
messages.body_plain:
You can use the function plot.pxg() to look at the phenotype
as a function of the genotype at a marker or markers.

Alternatively, you could look at the contingency table.  You'd
have to get access to the relevant bits in the cross object,
or read in the data in the more usual matrix form and work with
it directly.

If I had a cross called "mycross" and I wanted to look at a table
of the genotype of marker "D13Mit90" against the 3rd phenotype,
I could do the following:

   g <- pull.geno(mycross)[,"D13Mit90"]
   y <- mycross$pheno[,3]

   table(y, g)

For an intercross, the genotypes in g get coded as 1,2,3 for
AA,AB,BB, respectively.

karl
